mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over three months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals a demand recovery in consumer durables, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the average rank IC falls below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) rises above its 12-month moving average signals a tight labor market, increasing wage pressures and cost-push inflation, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, reducing corporate revenue growth and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the average rank IC is above 0.20.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for six consecutive months signals a deflationary environment, lowering real interest rates and supporting equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change < 0.2% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically distinguishable from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average while personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) stagnate signals increased precautionary savings, reducing near-term demand and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average rank IC is above 0.15.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, depressing consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based expansion in manufacturing and construction, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the average rank IC is below 0.10.
